dedupe_keys.name: australia s submarine telecommunication cable locations and protection zones 2021

description: This dataset maps the submarine telecommunication cables inside Australia's three cable protection zones as they stood in 2021, from spreadsheets the Australian Communications and Media Authority provided to Geoscience Australia. ACMA declares protection zones over cables of national significance: two off Sydney, the Northern Sydney zone from Narrabeen Beach and the Southern Sydney zone from Tamarama and Clovelly beaches, protecting branches of the Australia Japan Cable and the Southern Cross Cable, and one off Perth from City Beach, protecting the SEA-ME-WE 3 cable to South East Asia, the Middle East and Western Europe. Each zone runs from the shore to a depth of 2,000 metres and one nautical mile either side of the cable, and the Sydney zones also include the area between adjacent cables; within them, activities that risk damaging cables, such as anchoring and some fishing, are prohibited or restricted, with penalties for damage. Coverage: the three protection zones, current as of 2021. Format and access: WMS and WFS services on the CSIRO GeoServer, listed on data.gov.au through the Australian Ocean Data Network, free; the portal gives the licence as not specified with a CC BY 4.0 badge. Caveats: only cables inside protection zones are included; newer cables landed after 2021 are missing. Simulation uses: hazard exposure of cable landings to anchors, fishing and coastal hazards, and network models of Australia's international connectivity. Related records: TeleGeography's submarine cable map covers all cables, and the ICPC works on cable protection.
